spot.description: Ad hoc or emergency supply at prevailing DMPR wholesale or negotiated price. No volume commitment. Suited for urgent or top-up procurement.

term_contract.description: 12â€“36 month supply agreements with fixed delivery schedules and volume commitments. Government entities typically use 2-year terms; SOEs use 5-year frameworks. Requires DMRE wholesale licence, ISO certification, and valid BEE certificate.
term_contract.typical_duration: 12â€“36 months for municipalities; up to 60 months for SOEs

framework_agreement.description: Multi-supplier panel model used by large SOEs and metros. Pre-qualified suppliers receive volume allocations by the buyer on a rotational or quota basis. Eskom's R21bn contract used this structure with panel suppliers including Astron Energy, Lanele Resources, Nutinox, African Forwarding and Shipping, and Severino Industries (awarded December 2024).

typical_volume_thresholds.eskom_ocgt_scale: Up to 1,000,000,000 litres over a 5-year contract period

contract_structures.pricing_mechanism: Most tenders reference the DMPR coastal or inland wholesale price at the time of delivery, with a logistics and delivery differential negotiated per delivery zone. Some framework contracts use a fixed margin above the DMPR price rather than a fixed rand-per-litre price.
contract_structures.payment_terms: 30â€“60 days EFT is standard for government entities. Eskom OCGT contract required 60-day payment terms with significant working capital (minimum ~R100m stock on hand) required from suppliers.

largest_diesel_procurers.estimated_volume: Up to 1 billion litres over 5 years for OCGT peaking plants alone
